title: Add Zabbix protocol dissector
description:
[Zabbix](https://www.zabbix.com/) is a monitoring application that uses its own protocols for communicating between various Zabbix components: Zabbix servers, proxies and agents/senders. This dissector supports the protocols as defined in https://www.zabbix.com/documentation/current/en/manual/appendix/protocols.

This is based on the Lua dissectors at https://github.com/markkuleinio/wireshark-zabbix-dissectors.

Features:
- Supports TCP desegmenting, compression and TLS
- Dissects both passive agent connections (10050/tcp, plaintext-based) and active agent, proxy and sender/trapper connections (10051/tcp, JSON-based), ports are configurable
- Detects passive agent conversations by checking the request being non-JSON (not depending on the well-known TCP ports)
- Calculates response times (`zabbix.time`) using protocol data saved in conversations
- Detects the connection type (proxy, agent, sender/trapper) based on the JSON data contents
- Shows the interesting fields in the dissection tree, updates Info column and Zabbix tree item text based on connection type
- Dissects protocols up to Zabbix version 6.4 (currently latest release) and 7.0 (currently in alpha)
  - However, does **not** support _passive_ agent connections in Zabbix 3.x or earlier (= without the Zabbix protocol header; _active_ agent connections are dissected in those very old versions as well; note that Zabbix 4.0 was released already in 2018)

Sample captures:
- Zabbix 7.0.0alpha2 server, proxy and agent 2: [zabbix70-proxy-and-agent.pcapng](/uploads/cc0dc2f2df44ebe4a6e76371a06a359a/zabbix70-proxy-and-agent.pcapng)
- Zabbix 3.0.32 (very old!) server, proxy and agent: [zabbix30-proxy-and-agent.pcapng](/uploads/0165d6443b846055237734564148e56f/zabbix30-proxy-and-agent.pcapng)
- (more samples can be downloaded in the Lua dissector GitHub repo linked above)

This is my first C dissector I've built from ground up, so all comments are welcome.

This introduced a startup crash when built with ASAN. Fixed in !11518.

So there are lots of learning opportunities for me I see 🤔😀

 `tokens` is defined, allocated and used as:

```
    jsmntok_t *tokens = wmem_alloc_array(pinfo->pool, jsmntok_t, token_count);
    int ret = json_parse(json_str, tokens, token_count);
```

I have been under impression that any memory allocations done by `wmem` functions are automatically freed after the defined scope ceases to exist (in this case packet scope, when `pinfo->pool` is used, right?).

Is this a false alarm, or how do you suggest I should modify the code?
May be a false positive (and yes coveritday don't like wmem function...)

commits_data.title: Add Zabbix protocol dissector
commits_data.message:
Add Zabbix protocol dissector

Features:
- Supports also compressed and TLS-encrypted Zabbix connections as well
  as TCP desegmenting
- Dissects both passive agent connections (10050/tcp, plaintext-based)
  and active agent, proxy and sender/trapper connections (10051/tcp,
  JSON-based), ports are configurable
- Detects passive agent conversations by checking the request being
  non-JSON (not depending on the well-known TCP ports)
- Calculates response times using protocol data saved in conversations
- Detects the connection type (proxy, agent, sender/trapper) and shows
  tree and Info column information accordingly
- Dissects protocols up to Zabbix version 6.4 (currently latest) and
  7.0 (currently in alpha)
- Does not support passive agent connections in Zabbix 3.x or earlier
  (it does not have the normal Zabbix header; note that Zabbix 4.0 was
  released in 2018)
